revision.text:
{{神社 |名称 = 篠岡八幡大神社 |画像={{画像募集中|cat=さいたま市}} |所在地 = [[埼玉県]][[さいたま市]][[岩槻区]][[大戸 (さいたま市岩槻区)|大戸]]1752 |地図 = |祭神 = [[オモダル・アヤカシコネ|面足尊・吾屋惶根尊]] |社格 = 村社 |創建 = [[天明]]2年（[[1782年]]） |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = |神事 = }} '''武蔵第六天神社'''（むさしだいろくてんじんじゃ）は、[[埼玉県]][[さいたま市]][[岩槻区]]の[[神社]]。
== 歴史 == [[1782年]]（[[天明]]2年）に創建された。ただそれ以前から[[祠]]として存在しており、[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には、領主の[[太田氏]]をはじめ、近隣住民の信仰を集めていた<ref name="当社">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ 御由緒]武蔵第六天神社</ref>。
当社はあらゆる災難を取り除き、家内安全、五穀豊穣を叶える神社とされている。このように[[功徳|ご利益]]が広範囲にわたっていることから、[[武蔵国]]（[[埼玉県]]・[[東京都]]）のみならず、[[関東地方|関東一円]]から多くの参詣者が訪れる。また[[祭神]]の「面'''足'''尊」から足の病気を治す神様としても信仰を集め、最近では[[交通安全]]の神ともされている<ref name="当社"></ref><ref name="散歩">大村進 著『埼玉ふるさと散歩（岩槻市）』さきたま出版会、1992年、111p</ref>。
[[明治]]の[[近代社格制度]]では、当初は「無格社」であった。しかし[[1907年]]（明治40年）に村社の香取神社を始めとする4社が合祀され、村社となった<ref name="当社"></ref>。
多くの参詣者が訪れることから、当社の周辺には川魚料理の店が多い<ref name="散歩"></ref>。
== 交通アクセス == *[[路線バス]]大戸停留所より徒歩13分。

鳥居と拝殿 |所在地 = [[埼玉県]][[さいたま市]][[岩槻区]][[大戸 (さいたま市岩槻区)|大戸]]1752 |位置 = {{Coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E|type:landmark_region:JP-11|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[オモダル・アヤカシコネ|面足尊・吾屋惶根尊]] |社格 = 旧[[村社]] |創建 = [[天明]]2年（[[1782年]]） |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label=武蔵第六天神社|float=center|relief=1|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210|coord={{coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E}}}} }} '''武蔵第六天神社'''（むさしだいろくてんじんじゃ）は、[[埼玉県]][[さいたま市]][[岩槻区]]の[[神社]]。 == 歴史 == [[1782年]]（[[天明]]2年）に創建された。ただそれ以前から[[祠]]として存在しており、[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には、領主の[[太田氏]]をはじめ、近隣住民の信仰を集めていた[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ 御由緒]武蔵第六天神社。 当社はあらゆる災難を取り除き、家内安全、五穀豊穣を叶える神社とされている。このように[[功徳|ご利益]]が広範囲にわたっていることから、[[武蔵国]]（[[埼玉県]]・[[東京都]]）のみならず、[[関東地方|関東一円]]から多くの参詣者が訪れる。また[[祭神]]の「面'''足'''尊」から足の病気を治す神様としても信仰を集め、最近では[[交通安全]]の神ともされている大村進 著『埼玉ふるさと散歩（岩槻市）』さきたま出版会、1992年、111p。 [[明治]]の[[近代社格制度]]では、当初は「無格社」であった。しかし[[1907年]]（明治40年）に村社の香取神社を始めとする4社が合祀され、村社となった。 多くの参詣者が訪れることから、当社の周辺には川魚料理の店が多い。 File:Road to Musashi Dairokuten Jinja.JPG|当社に至るまでの道（川魚料理店がある） == 交通アクセス == *[[路線バス]]大戸停留所より徒歩13分。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == *大村進 著『埼玉ふるさと散歩（岩槻市）』[[さきたま出版会]]、1992年 == 外部リンク == * [https://dairokuten.or.jp/ 武蔵第六天神社] - 公式サイト {{Pref-stub|pref=埼玉県}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:むさしたいろくてんしんしや}} [[Category:さいたま市の神社]] [[Category:岩槻区の歴史]] [[Category:岩槻区の建築物]] [[Category:埼玉県の旧村社]]

Dairokuten Shrine forks [[Category:Dairokuten Shrine forks]][[category:new pages]]
== Major Sixth Heaven Shrines (第六天神社) == The following is a list of notable shrines with the name "Sixth Heaven" (第六天 or 大六天) that still exist today. These shrines are predominantly found in the {{ill|Kantō region|ja|関東地方}}, though they can also be seen in the {{ill|Tōhoku region|ja|東北地方}} and parts of the {{ill|Chūbu region|ja|中部地方}} (including {{ill|Kōshin'etsu|ja|甲信越}}<ref name="dairokuten-koushinetsu">Reference: [https://ameblo.jp/soubu-nakamiti/entry-11978770465.html Kōshin’etsu and Jōetsu Dairokuten Map] (Exploring Dōsojin and Dairokuten).</ref> and {{ill|Tōkai region|ja|東海地方}}, specifically {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|ja|静岡県}}). However, west of {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|ja|長野県}} and Shizuoka Prefecture, these shrines are scarcely found.
According to {{ill|corporate registry|ja|法人登記}}, there are 36 registered religious corporations with names that include variations of "Sixth Heaven": 19 as "Dairokuten Jinja," 4 as "Dairokuten Sha," 1 as "Dairokuten Miya," 2 as "Dairokusha," 5 as "Dairokuten Jinja" (using the kanji 大六天), 3 as "Dairokusha" (大六天社), and 2 as "Maōten Jinja." None of these include place names in their official titles. For instance, {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Jinja|ja|武蔵第六天神社}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|ja|第六天榊神社}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Jinja" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. Shrines with religious corporation status are marked with a ☆ below.
=== Tōhoku Region === ; Miyagi Prefecture [[File:Dairokuten jinjya (Natori, Miyagi) 01.jpg|thumb|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori City, Miyagi Prefecture)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Misato)|ja|大六天神社 (美里町)}} ({{ill|Tōda District|ja|遠田郡}}, Misato Town, Nigo Chiyokubo No. 2) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori)|ja|第六天神社 (名取市)}} ({{ill|Natori City|ja|名取市}}, Masuda Town) ☆ - The shrine's origin is linked to the enshrinement of seven celestial deities ({{ill|Kamiyo Nanayo|ja|神世七代}}) in the former Masuda Village, with the sixth deity, "Uma-tsuka Myōjin" (present-day main enshrined deities are {{ill|Omotaru no Mikoto|ja|オモダル・アヤカシコネ}}), being dedicated here.<ref name="miyagi-jinjacho-natori-dairokuten"/><ref name="natori100sen-dairokuten"/> Seven shrines still exist in the town today.<ref>[http://www.city.natori.miyagi.jp/public/masuda-kou/tenzinsya.html Masuda's Seven Shrines] (Natori City Masuda Community Center: Cultural Properties and Historical Sites).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Sendai)|ja|大六天神社 (仙台市)}} ({{ill|Sendai City|ja|仙台市}}, {{ill|Aoba-ku|ja|青葉区}}, Ōkura)
; Fukushima Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Kōriyama)|ja|大六天魔王神社 (郡山市)}} ({{ill|Kōriyama City|ja|郡山市}}, Tamuramachi, Kanazawa Dairoku) Known as "Maō Shrine" - The shrine's signboard displays "Dairokuten Maō Jinja," while the torii bears the name "Maō Shrine."<ref>[https://ameblo.jp/miyamoto-gotoh/entry-12650137834.html Dairokuten Maō Shrine Goshuin, Kōriyama City, Tamuramachi] (Ameba Blog: Shrine Pilgrimages, January 14, 2021).</ref>
=== Kantō Region === ; Gunma Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten (Minakami)|ja|大六天 (みなかみ町)}} ({{ill|Tone District|ja|利根郡}}, Minakami Town, Fujiwara)<ref name="dairokuten-koushinetsu"/>
; Tochigi Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Jingū (Mōka)|ja|第六天神宮 (茂木町)}} ({{ill|Haga District|ja|芳賀郡}}, Mōka Town, Tenko) * {{ill|Yamakura Dairokutenō Jinja|ja|山倉大六天王神社}} ({{ill|Mooka City|ja|真岡市}}, Kamionuma)
; Ibaraki Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Goka Esegawa)|ja|第六天神社 (五霞町江川)}} ({{ill|Sashima District|ja|猿島郡}}, Goka Town, Esegawa) ☆ * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Goka Kōshu)|ja|第六天神社 (五霞町幸主)}} (Goka Town, Kōshu) ☆ * {{ill|Kōmusubi Jinja (Bandō)|ja|皇産霊神社 (坂東市)}} ({{ill|Bandō City|ja|坂東市}}, Ōsaki) Known as "Dairokuten Jinja" ☆ * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Tsukuba)|ja|大六天神社 (つくば市)}} ({{ill|Tsukuba City|ja|つくば市}}, Onigakubo)

; Tokyo [[File:DairokutenSakakiJinja.JPG|thumb|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja (Taitō City, Tokyo)]] [[File:Dairokuten-mao jinjya (Hachioji).JPG|thumb|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Hachiōji City, Tokyo)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|ja|第六天榊神社}} ({{ill|Taitō City|ja|台東区}}, Kuramae) Also called "Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja" ☆ * {{ill|Dairokuten Sha (Meguro)|ja|第六天社 (目黒区)}} ({{ill|Meguro City|ja|目黒区}}, Kamimeguro) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Suginami)|ja|第六天神社 (杉並区)}} ({{ill|Suginami City|ja|杉並区}}, Takaito-nishi) Also called "Dairokuten Jinja" ☆ * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Nakano)|ja|第六天神社 (中野区)}} ({{ill|Nakano City|ja|中野区}}, Higashinakano) * {{ill|Ōrokuten Sha (Setagaya)|ja|大六天社 (世田谷区)}} ({{ill|Setagaya City|ja|世田谷区}}, Ōkura) * {{ill|Enoki Dairokuten Jinja|ja|榎大六天神}} ({{ill|Itabashi City|ja|板橋区}}, Honchō) * {{ill|Ōrokuten Negishi Jinja|ja|大六天根岸神社}} ({{ill|Ōta City|ja|大田区}}, Ōmori-kita) * {{ill|Dairokuten Negahara Jinja|ja|代六天根ヶ原神社}} (Ōta City, Sannō) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Kunitachi)|ja|第六天神社 (国立市)}} ({{ill|Kunitachi City|ja|国立市}}, Yaho) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Tachikawa)|ja|第六天神社 (立川市)}} ({{ill|Tachikawa City|ja|立川市}}, Nishikichō) ☆ * {{ill|Ōrokuten Jinja (Hachiōji)|ja|大六天神社 (八王子市)}} ({{ill|Hachiōji City|ja|八王子市}}, Inumemachi) * {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Hachiōji)|ja|大六天魔王神社 (八王子市)}} (Hachiōji City, Motohachiōji-machi) * {{ill|Ōrokuten Sha (Machida, Aihara)|ja|大六天社 (町田市相原)}} ({{ill|Machida City|ja|町田市}}, Aihara-machi) Also called "Ōto Dairokuten Sha" ☆ <ref>[https://tesshow.jp/tama/machida/shrine_aihara_dairok.html Ōto Dairokuten Sha / Machida City, Aihara-machi Shrine] (Cat's Footsteps).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Machida, Tsuruma)|ja|第六天神社 (町田市鶴間)}} (Machida City, Tsuruma)

{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Jinja|en]][[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|en]][[ja:第六天榊神社]] are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Jinja" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. Shrines with religious corporation status are marked with a ☆ below. === Tōhoku Region === ; Miyagi Prefecture [[File:Dairokuten jinjya (Natori, Miyagi) 01.jpg|thumb|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori City, Miyagi Prefecture)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Misato)|en]][[ja:大六天神社 (美里町)]] ({{ill|Tōda District|en]][[ja:遠田郡]], Misato Town, Nigo Chiyokubo No. 2) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori)|en]][[ja:第六天神社 (名取市)]] ({{ill|Natori City|en]][[ja:名取市]], Masuda Town) ☆ - The shrine's origin is linked to the enshrinement of seven celestial deities ({{ill|Kamiyo Nanayo|en]][[ja:神世七代]]) in the former Masuda Village, with the sixth deity, "Uma-tsuka Myōjin" (present-day main enshrined deities are {{ill|Omotaru no Mikoto|en]][[ja:オモダル・アヤカシコネ]]), being dedicated here.<ref name="miyagi-jinjacho-natori-dairokuten"/><ref name="natori100sen-dairokuten"/> Seven shrines still exist in the town today.<ref>[http://www.city.natori.miyagi.jp/public/masuda-kou/tenzinsya.html Masuda's Seven Shrines] (Natori City Masuda Community Center: Cultural Properties and Historical Sites).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Sendai)|en]][[ja:大六天神社 (仙台市)]] ({{ill|Sendai City|en]][[ja:仙台市]], {{ill|Aoba-ku|en]][[ja:青葉区]], Ōkura)
; Fukushima Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Kōriyama)|en]][[ja:大六天魔王神社 (郡山市)]] ({{ill|Kōriyama City|en]][[ja:郡山市]], Tamuramachi, Kanazawa Dairoku) Known as "Maō Shrine" - The shrine's signboard displays "Dairokuten Maō Jinja," while the torii bears the name "Maō Shrine."<ref>[https://ameblo.jp/miyamoto-gotoh/entry-12650137834.html Dairokuten Maō Shrine Goshuin, Kōriyama City, Tamuramachi] (Ameba Blog: Shrine Pilgrimages, January 14, 2021).</ref>
=== Kantō Region === ; Gunma Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten (Minakami)|en]][[ja:大六天 (みなかみ町)]] ({{ill|Tone District|en]][[ja:利根郡]], Minakami Town, Fujiwara)<ref name="dairokuten-koushinetsu">Reference: [https://ameblo.jp/soubu-nakamiti/entry-11978770465.html Kōshin’etsu and Jōetsu Dairokuten Map] (Exploring Dōsojin and Dairokuten).</ref>
; Tochigi Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Jingū (Mōka)|en]][[ja:第六天神宮 (茂木町)]] ({{ill|Haga District|en]][[ja:芳賀郡]], Mōka Town, Tenko) * {{ill|Yamakura Dairokutenō Jinja|en]][[ja:山倉大六天王神社]] ({{ill|Mooka City|en]][[ja:真岡市]], Kamionuma)

; Tokyo [[File:DairokutenSakakiJinja.JPG|thumb|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja (Taitō City, Tokyo)]] [[File:Dairokuten-mao jinjya (Hachioji).JPG|thumb|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Hachiōji City, Tokyo)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|en]][[ja:第六天榊神社]] ({{ill|Taitō City|en]][[ja:台東区]], Kuramae) Also called "Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja" ☆ * {{ill|Dairokuten Sha (Meguro)|en]][[ja:第六天社 (目黒区)]] ({{ill|Meguro City|en]][[ja:目黒区]], Kamimeguro) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Suginami)|en]][[ja:第六天神社 (杉並区)]] ({{ill|Suginami City|en]][[ja:杉並区]], Takaito-nishi) Also called "Dairokuten Jinja" ☆ * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Nakano)|en]][[ja:第六天神社 (中野区)]] ({{ill|Nakano City|en]][[ja:中野区]], Higashinakano) * {{ill|Ōrokuten Sha (Setagaya)|en]][[ja:大六天社 (世田谷区)]] ({{ill|Setagaya City|en]][[ja:世田谷区]], Ōkura) * {{ill|Enoki Dairokuten Jinja|en]][[ja:榎大六天神]] ({{ill|Itabashi City|en]][[ja:板橋区]], Honchō) * {{ill|Ōrokuten Negishi Jinja|en]][[ja:大六天根岸神社]] ({{ill|Ōta City|en]][[ja:大田区]], Ōmori-kita) * {{ill|Dairokuten Negahara Jinja|en]][[ja:代六天根ヶ原神社]] (Ōta City, Sannō) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Kunitachi)|en]][[ja:第六天神社 (国立市)]] ({{ill|Kunitachi City|en]][[ja:国立市]], Yaho) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Tachikawa)|en]][[ja:第六天神社 (立川市)]] ({{ill|Tachikawa City|en]][[ja:立川市]], Nishikichō) ☆ * {{ill|Ōrokuten Jinja (Hachiōji)|en]][[ja:大六天神社 (八王子市)]] ({{ill|Hachiōji City|en]][[ja:八王子市]], Inumemachi) * {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Hachiōji)|en]][[ja:大六天魔王神社 (八王子市)]] (Hachiōji City, Motohachiōji-machi) * {{ill|Ōrokuten Sha (Machida, Aihara)|en]][[ja:大六天社 (町田市相原)]] ({{ill|Machida City|en]][[ja:町田市]], Aihara-machi) Also called "Ōto Dairokuten Sha" ☆ <ref>[https://tesshow.jp/tama/machida/shrine_aihara_dairok.html Ōto Dairokuten Sha / Machida City, Aihara-machi Shrine] (Cat's Footsteps).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Machida, Tsuruma)|en]][[ja:第六天神社 (町田市鶴間)]] (Machida City, Tsuruma)

[[Category:Dairokuten Shrine forks]][[category:new pages]]
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Jinja|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:第六天榊神社]] are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Jinja" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. Shrines with religious corporation status are marked with a ☆ below. === Tōhoku Region === ; Miyagi Prefecture [[File:Dairokuten jinjya (Natori, Miyagi) 01.jpg|thumb|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori City, Miyagi Prefecture)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Misato)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天神社 (美里町)]] ({{ill|Tōda District|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:遠田郡]], Misato Town, Nigo Chiyokubo No. 2) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:第六天神社 (名取市)]] ({{ill|Natori City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:名取市]], Masuda Town) ☆ - The shrine's origin is linked to the enshrinement of seven celestial deities ({{ill|Kamiyo Nanayo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:神世七代]]) in the former Masuda Village, with the sixth deity, "Uma-tsuka Myōjin" (present-day main enshrined deities are {{ill|Omotaru no Mikoto|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:オモダル・アヤカシコネ]]), being dedicated here.<ref name="miyagi-jinjacho-natori-dairokuten"/><ref name="natori100sen-dairokuten"/> Seven shrines still exist in the town today.<ref>[http://www.city.natori.miyagi.jp/public/masuda-kou/tenzinsya.html Masuda's Seven Shrines] (Natori City Masuda Community Center: Cultural Properties and Historical Sites).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天神社 (仙台市)]] ({{ill|Sendai City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:仙台市]], {{ill|Aoba-ku|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:青葉区]], Ōkura)
; Fukushima Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Kōriyama)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天魔王神社 (郡山市)]] ({{ill|Kōriyama City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:郡山市]], Tamuramachi, Kanazawa Dairoku) Known as "Maō Shrine" - The shrine's signboard displays "Dairokuten Maō Jinja," while the torii bears the name "Maō Shrine."<ref>[https://ameblo.jp/miyamoto-gotoh/entry-12650137834.html Dairokuten Maō Shrine Goshuin, Kōriyama City, Tamuramachi] (Ameba Blog: Shrine Pilgrimages, [[Category:January]][[Category:Search created pages]][[Category:New pages]] 14, 2021).</ref>

[[Category:Dairokuten Shrine forks]][[category:new pages]]
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Jinja|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:第六天榊神社]] are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Jinja" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. Shrines with religious corporation status are marked with a ☆ below. === Tōhoku Region === ; Miyagi Prefecture [[File:Dairokuten jinjya (Natori, Miyagi) 01.jpg|thumb|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori City, Miyagi Prefecture)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Misato)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天神社 (美里町)]] ({{ill|Tōda District|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:遠田郡]], Misato Town, Nigo Chiyokubo No. 2) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:第六天神社 (名取市)]] ({{ill|Natori City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:名取市]], Masuda Town) ☆ - The shrine's origin is linked to the enshrinement of seven celestial deities ({{ill|Kamiyo Nanayo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:神世七代]]) in the former Masuda Village, with the sixth deity, "Uma-tsuka Myōjin" (present-day main enshrined deities are {{ill|Omotaru no Mikoto|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:オモダル・アヤカシコネ]]), being dedicated here.<ref name="miyagi-jinjacho-natori-dairokuten"/><ref name="natori100sen-dairokuten"/> Seven shrines still exist in the town today.<ref>[http://www.city.natori.miyagi.jp/public/masuda-kou/tenzinsya.html Masuda's Seven Shrines] (Natori City Masuda Community Center: Cultural Properties and Historical Sites).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天神社 (仙台市)]] ({{ill|Sendai City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:仙台市]], {{ill|Aoba-ku|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:青葉区]], Ōkura)
; Fukushima Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Kōriyama)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天魔王神社 (郡山市)]] ({{ill|Kōriyama City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:郡山市]], Tamuramachi, Kanazawa Dairoku) Known as "Maō Shrine" - The shrine's signboard displays "Dairokuten Maō Jinja," while the torii bears the name "Maō Shrine."<ref>[https://ameblo.jp/miyamoto-gotoh/entry-12650137834.html Dairokuten Maō Shrine Goshuin, Kōriyama City, Tamuramachi] (Ameba Blog: Shrine Pilgrimages, [[Category:January]][[Category:Search created pages]][[Category:New pages]] 14, 2021).</ref>

[[Category:Dairokuten Shrine forks]][[category:new pages]]
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Jinja|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:第六天榊神社]] are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Jinja" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. Shrines with religious corporation status are marked with a ☆ below. === Tōhoku Region === ; Miyagi Prefecture [[File:Dairokuten jinjya (Natori, Miyagi) 01.jpg|thumb|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori City, Miyagi Prefecture)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Misato)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天神社 (美里町)]] ({{ill|Tōda District|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:遠田郡]], Misato Town, Nigo Chiyokubo No. 2) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:第六天神社 (名取市)]] ({{ill|Natori City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:名取市]], Masuda Town) ☆ - The shrine's origin is linked to the enshrinement of seven celestial deities ({{ill|Kamiyo Nanayo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:神世七代]]) in the former Masuda Village, with the sixth deity, "Uma-tsuka Myōjin" (present-day main enshrined deities are {{ill|Omotaru no Mikoto|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:オモダル・アヤカシコネ]]), being dedicated here.<ref name="miyagi-jinjacho-natori-dairokuten"/><ref name="natori100sen-dairokuten"/> Seven shrines still exist in the town today.<ref>[http://www.city.natori.miyagi.jp/public/masuda-kou/tenzinsya.html Masuda's Seven Shrines] (Natori City Masuda Community Center: Cultural Properties and Historical Sites).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天神社 (仙台市)]] ({{ill|Sendai City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:仙台市]], {{ill|Aoba-ku|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:青葉区]], Ōkura)
; Fukushima Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Kōriyama)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天魔王神社 (郡山市)]] ({{ill|Kōriyama City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:郡山市]], Tamuramachi, Kanazawa Dairoku) Known as "Maō Shrine" - The shrine's signboard displays "Dairokuten Maō Jinja," while the torii bears the name "Maō Shrine."<ref>[https://ameblo.jp/miyamoto-gotoh/entry-12650137834.html Dairokuten Maō Shrine Goshuin, Kōriyama City, Tamuramachi] (Ameba Blog: Shrine Pilgrimages, [[Category:January]][[Category:Search created pages]][[Category:New pages]] 14, 2021).</ref>

[[Category:Dairokuten Shrines]] [[category:new pages]]
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Jinja|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:第六天榊神社]] are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Jinja" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. Shrines with religious corporation status are marked with a ☆ below. === Tōhoku Region === ; Miyagi Prefecture [[File:Dairokuten jinjya (Natori, Miyagi) 01.jpg|thumb|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori City, Miyagi Prefecture)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Misato)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天神社 (美里町)]] ({{ill|Tōda District|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:遠田郡]], Misato Town, Nigo Chiyokubo No. 2) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:第六天神社 (名取市)]] ({{ill|Natori City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:名取市]], Masuda Town) ☆ - The shrine's origin is linked to the enshrinement of seven celestial deities ({{ill|Kamiyo Nanayo|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:神世七代]]) in the former Masuda Village, with the sixth deity, "Uma-tsuka Myōjin" (present-day main enshrined deities are {{ill|Omotaru no Mikoto|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:オモダル・アヤカシコネ]]), being dedicated here.<ref name="miyagi-jinjacho-natori-dairokuten"/><ref name="natori100sen-dairokuten"/> Seven shrines still exist in the town today.<ref>[http://www.city.natori.miyagi.jp/public/masuda-kou/tenzinsya.html Masuda's Seven Shrines] (Natori City Masuda Community Center: Cultural Properties and Historical Sites).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:大六天神社 (仙台市)]] ({{ill|Sendai City|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:仙台市]], {{ill|Aoba-ku|en}}[[Category:New pages]][[Category:new pages]][[ja:青葉区]], Ōkura)

[[Category:Dairokuten Shrines]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Jinja|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:第六天榊神社]] are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Jinja" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. Shrines with religious corporation status are marked with a ☆ below. === Tōhoku Region === ; Miyagi Prefecture [[File:Dairokuten jinjya (Natori, Miyagi) 01.jpg|thumb|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori City, Miyagi Prefecture)]] * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Misato)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大六天神社 (美里町)]] ({{ill|Tōda District|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:遠田郡]], Misato Town, Nigo Chiyokubo No. 2) * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Natori)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:第六天神社 (名取市)]] ({{ill|Natori City|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:名取市]], Masuda Town) ☆ - The shrine's origin is linked to the enshrinement of seven celestial deities ({{ill|Kamiyo Nanayo|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:神世七代]]) in the former Masuda Village, with the sixth deity, "Uma-tsuka Myōjin" (present-day main enshrined deities are {{ill|Omotaru no Mikoto|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:オモダル・アヤカシコネ]]), being dedicated here.<ref name="miyagi-jinjacho-natori-dairokuten"/><ref name="natori100sen-dairokuten"/> Seven shrines still exist in the town today.<ref>[http://www.city.natori.miyagi.jp/public/masuda-kou/tenzinsya.html Masuda's Seven Shrines] (Natori City Masuda Community Center: Cultural Properties and Historical Sites).</ref> * {{ill|Dairokuten Jinja (Sendai)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大六天神社 (仙台市)]] ({{ill|Sendai City|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:仙台市]], {{ill|Aoba-ku|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:青葉区]], Ōkura)
; Fukushima Prefecture * {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Kōriyama)|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:大六天魔王神社 (郡山市)]] ({{ill|Kōriyama City|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]][[ja:郡山市]], Tamuramachi, Kanazawa Dairoku) Known as "Maō Shrine" - The shrine's signboard displays "Dairokuten Maō Jinja," while the torii bears the name "Maō Shrine."<ref>[https://ameblo.jp/miyamoto-gotoh/entry-12650137834.html Dairokuten Maō Shrine Goshuin, Kōriyama City, Tamuramachi] (Ameba Blog: Shrine Pilgrimages, [[Category:January]][[Category:Search created pages]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] 14, 2021).</ref>

[[Category:Dairokuten Shrines]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Musashi Dairokuten Jinja-qq]] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Jinja|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Musashi Dairokuten Jinja-qq]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Musashi Dairokuten Jinja-qq]] [[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Jinja|en}}[[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Musashi Dairokuten Jinja-qq]] [[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Musashi Dairokuten Jinja-qq]] [[ja:第六天榊神社]] are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Jinja" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. {{infobox religious building | Name = {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}} | Image = [[File:Musashi Dairokuten Jinja 01.JPG|250px]]
{{ill|Torii and Haiden|ja|鳥居と拝殿}} | Location = {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}{{ill|Saitama City|ja|さいたま市}}{{ill|Iwatsuki Ward|ja|岩槻区}}{{ill|Oodo (Saitama City, Iwatsuki Ward)|ja|大戸 (さいたま市岩槻区)|lt=Oodo (Saitama City, Iwatsuki Ward)|lt_ja=大戸}}1752 | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E|type:landmark_region:JP-11|display=inline,title}} | Enshrined Deity = {{ill|Menashison / Uwya Kashijoushin|ja|オモダル・アヤカシコネ|lt=Menashison / Uwya Kashijoushin|lt_ja=面足尊・吾屋惶根尊}} | Shrine Rank = Former {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社}} | Established = {{ill|Tenmei Era|ja|天明}}2年（{{ill|1782|ja|1782年}}） | Main Hall = | Alternate Name = | Markers, etc. = | Annual Festival = | Rituals = | Map = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}}|float=center|relief=1|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210|coord={{coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E}}}} }} '''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}, {{ill|Saitama City|ja|さいたま市}}, {{ill|Iwatsuki Ward|ja|岩槻区}}. {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. [[sn:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine}} [[sn:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine}} [[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] == History == During the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|ja|神仏習合}}, this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天}}), and was founded in {{ill|1782|ja|1782年}} (the 2nd year of the {{ill|Tenmei Era|ja|天明}}). However, even before that it existed as a {{ill|hokora|ja|祠}}, and during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|lt=Sengoku Period|lt_ja=戦国時代}} it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the {{ill|Ota Clan|ja|太田氏}}.[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{ill|History|ja|御由緒}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}} This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its {{ill|Merit|ja|功徳|lt=Benefit|lt_ja=ご利益}} extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former {{ill|Musashi Province|ja|武蔵国}} ({{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}} and {{ill|Tokyo Metropolis|ja|東京都}}) but from throughout the entire {{ill|Kanto Region|ja|関東地方|lt=Kanto Area|lt_ja=関東一円}}. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of {{ill|Traffic Safety|ja|交通安全}}.Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p Under the {{ill|Meiji Era|ja|明治}}’s {{ill|Modern Shrine Ranking System|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in {{ill|1907|ja|1907年}} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine. Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine. File:Road to Musashi Dairokuten Jinja.JPG|The road leading to this shrine (with river fish restaurants) == Transportation Access == * A 13‑minute walk from the {{ill|Route Bus|ja|路線バス}} stop at {{ill|Oodo Bus Stop|ja|大戸停留所}}. == Footnotes == {{Footnote Help}} {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, {{ill|Sakitama Publishing Association|ja|さきたま出版会}}, 1992 == External Links == * [https://dairokuten.or.jp/ {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}}] - Official Website {{Pref-stub|pref=埼玉県}} {{shinto-stub}} '''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) [[category:completion tier 1]] [[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] [[Category:Shrines of Saitama City]] [[Category:History of Iwatsuki Ward]] [[Category:Buildings in Iwatsuki Ward]] [[Category:Former Village Shrines of Saitama Prefecture]] [[Category:completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine]][[Category:qq]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine}}[[Category:qq]]

However, even before that it existed as a {{ill|hokora|ja|祠}}, and during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|lt=Sengoku Period|lt_ja=戦国時代}} it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the {{ill|Ota Clan|ja|太田氏}}.[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{ill|History|ja|御由緒}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}} This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its {{ill|Merit|ja|功徳|lt=Benefit|lt_ja=ご利益}} extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former {{ill|Musashi Province|ja|武蔵国}} ({{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}} and {{ill|Tokyo Metropolis|ja|東京都}}) but from throughout the entire {{ill|Kanto Region|ja|関東地方|lt=Kanto Area|lt_ja=関東一円}}. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of {{ill|Traffic Safety|ja|交通安全}}.Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p Under the {{ill|Meiji Era|ja|明治}}’s {{ill|Modern Shrine Ranking System|ja|近代社格制度}}, the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in {{ill|1907|ja|1907年}} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine. {{ill|Torii and Haiden|ja|鳥居と拝殿}} | Location = {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}{{ill|Saitama City|ja|さいたま市}}{{ill|Iwatsuki Ward|ja|岩槻区}}{{ill|Oodo (Saitama City, Iwatsuki Ward)|ja|大戸 (さいたま市岩槻区)|lt=Oodo (Saitama City, Iwatsuki Ward)|lt_ja=大戸}}1752 | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E|type:landmark_region:JP-11|display=inline,title}} | Enshrined Deity = {{ill|Menashison / Uwya Kashijoushin|ja|オモダル・アヤカシコネ|lt=Menashison / Uwya Kashijoushin|lt_ja=面足尊・吾屋惶根尊}} | Shrine Rank = Former {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社}} | Established = {{ill|Tenmei Era|ja|天明}}2年（{{ill|1782|ja|1782年}}） | Main Hall = | Alternate Name = | Markers, etc. = | Annual Festival = | Rituals = | Map = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}}|float=center|relief=1|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210|coord={{coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E}}}} |deity = {{ill|Omodaru and Ayakashikone|lt=Ayakashikone|lt=Ayakashikone|ja|阿夜訶志古泥神|lt=Omodaru and Ayakashikone}}/{{ill|Demon King of the Sixth Heaven|lt=Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|天魔|lt=Sixth Heavenly Demon King|lt_ja=第六天魔王|lt=Demon King of the Sixth Heaven (Dairokuten Mao)}} }} '''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}, {{ill|Saitama City|ja|さいたま市}}, {{ill|Iwatsuki Ward|ja|岩槻区}}. {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. [[sn:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine}} [[sn:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine}} [[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] == History == During the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|ja|神仏習合|1=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}, this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天}}), and was founded in {{ill|1782|ja|1782年}} (the 2nd year of the {{ill|Tenmei Era|ja|天明}}). However, even before that it existed as a {{ill|hokora|ja|祠}}, and during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|lt=Sengoku Period|lt_ja=戦国時代}} it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the {{ill|Ota Clan|ja|太田氏}}.[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{ill|History|ja|御由緒}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}} This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its {{ill|Merit|ja|功徳|lt=Benefit|lt_ja=ご利益}} extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former {{ill|Musashi Province|ja|武蔵国}} ({{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}} and {{ill|Tokyo Metropolis|ja|東京都}}) but from throughout the entire {{ill|Kanto Region|ja|関東地方|lt=Kanto Area|lt_ja=関東一円}}. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of {{ill|Traffic Safety|ja|交通安全}}.Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p Under the {{ill|Meiji Era|ja|明治}}’s {{ill|Modern Shrine Ranking System|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in {{ill|1907|ja|1907年}} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine. Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine. {{ill|Torii and Haiden|ja|鳥居と拝殿}} | Location = {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}{{ill|Saitama City|ja|さいたま市}}{{ill|Iwatsuki Ward|ja|岩槻区}}{{ill|Oodo (Saitama City, Iwatsuki Ward)|ja|大戸 (さいたま市岩槻区)|lt=Oodo (Saitama City, Iwatsuki Ward)|lt_ja=大戸}}1752 | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E|type:landmark_region:JP-11|display=inline,title}} | Enshrined Deity = {{ill|Menashison / Uwya Kashijoushin|ja|オモダル・アヤカシコネ|lt=Menashison / Uwya Kashijoushin|lt_ja=面足尊・吾屋惶根尊}} | Shrine Rank = Former {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社}} | Established = {{ill|Tenmei Era|ja|天明}}2nd year （{{ill|1782|ja|1782nd year }}） | Main Hall = | Alternate Name = | Markers, etc. = | Annual Festival = | Rituals = | Map = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}}|float=center|relief=1|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210|coord={{coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E}}}} |deity = {{ill|Omodaru and Ayakashikone|lt=Ayakashikone|lt=Ayakashikone|ja|阿夜訶志古泥神|lt=Omodaru and Ayakashikone}}/{{ill|Demon King of the Sixth Heaven|lt=Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|天魔|lt=Sixth Heavenly Demon King|lt_ja=第六天魔王|lt=Demon King of the Sixth Heaven (Dairokuten Mao)}} }} '''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}, {{ill|Saitama City|ja|さいたま市}}, {{ill|Iwatsuki Ward|ja|岩槻区}}. {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. [[sn:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine}} [[sn:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Musashi Dairokuten Shrine}} [[ja:武蔵第六天神社]] == History == During the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|ja|神仏習合|1=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}, this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天}}), and was founded in {{ill|1782|ja|1782nd year }} (the 2nd year of the {{ill|Tenmei Era|ja|天明}}). However, even before that it existed as a {{ill|hokora|ja|祠}}, and during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|lt=Sengoku Period|lt_ja=戦国時代}} it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the {{ill|Ota Clan|ja|太田氏}}.[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{ill|History|ja|御由緒}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}} This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its {{ill|Merit|ja|功徳|lt=Benefit|lt_ja=ご利益}} extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former {{ill|Musashi Province|ja|武蔵国}} ({{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}} and {{ill|Tokyo Metropolis|ja|東京都}}) but from throughout the entire {{ill|Kanto Region|ja|関東地方|lt=Kanto Area|lt_ja=関東一円}}. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of {{ill|Traffic Safety|ja|交通安全}}.Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p Under the {{ill|Meiji Era|ja|明治}}’s {{ill|Modern Shrine Ranking System|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in {{ill|1907|ja|1907th year }} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine. Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine. {{神社 |名称 = 武蔵第六天神社 |画像=[[File:Musashi Dairokuten Jinja 01.JPG|250px]]
鳥居と拝殿 |所在地 = [[埼玉県]][[さいたま市]][[岩槻区]][[大戸 (さいたま市岩槻区)|大戸]]1752 |位置 = {{Coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E|type:landmark_region:JP-11|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[オモダル・アヤカシコネ|面足尊・吾屋惶根尊]] |社格 = 旧[[村社]] |創建 = [[天明]]2年（[[1782年]]） |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label=武蔵第六天神社|float=center|relief=1|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210|coord={{coord|35|55|55|N|139|44|9|E}}}} }} '''武蔵第六天神社'''（むさしだいろくてんじんじゃ）は、[[埼玉県]][[さいたま市]][[岩槻区]]の[[神社]]。 == 歴史 == [[神仏習合]]時代に[[第六天魔王]]（[[他化自在天]]）を祀った[[第六天神社]]の1つであり、[[1782年]]（[[天明]]2年）に創建された。ただそれ以前から[[祠]]として存在しており、[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には、領主の[[太田氏]]をはじめ、近隣住民の信仰を集めていた[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ 御由緒]武蔵第六天神社。 当社はあらゆる災難を取り除き、家内安全、五穀豊穣を叶える神社とされている。このように[[功徳|ご利益]]が広範囲にわたっていることから、[[武蔵国]]（[[埼玉県]]・[[東京都]]）のみならず、[[関東地方|関東一円]]から多くの参詣者が訪れる。また[[祭神]]の「面'''足'''尊」から足の病気を治す神様としても信仰を集め、最近では[[交通安全]]の神ともされている大村進 著『埼玉ふるさと散歩（岩槻市）』さきたま出版会、1992年、111p。 [[明治]]の[[近代社格制度]]では、当初は「無格社」であった。しかし[[1907年]]（明治40年）に村社の香取神社を始めとする4社が合祀され、村社となった。 多くの参詣者が訪れることから、当社の周辺には川魚料理の店が多い。 File:Road to Musashi Dairokuten Jinja.JPG|当社に至るまでの道（川魚料理店がある） == 交通アクセス == *[[路線バス]]大戸停留所より徒歩13分。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == *大村進 著『埼玉ふるさと散歩（岩槻市）』[[さきたま出版会]]、1992年 == 外部リンク == * [https://dairokuten.or.jp/ 武蔵第六天神社] - 公式サイト {{Pref-stub|pref=埼玉県}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:むさしたいろくてんしんしや}} [[Category:さいたま市の神社]] [[Category:岩槻区の歴史]] [[Category:岩槻区の建築物]] [[Category:埼玉県の旧村社]]

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]], [[:en:Saitama (city)|Saitama City]], [[:en:Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|Iwatsuki Ward]].
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. 

== History ==
During the period of [[:en:Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]], this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|qq=|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in [[:en:1782|1782]] (the 2nd year of the [[:en:Tenmei|Tenmei Era]]). However, even before that it existed as a [[:en:Hokora|hokora]], and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku Period]] it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the [[:en:Ōta clan|Ota Clan]].<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its [[:en:Merit (Buddhism)|Benefit]] extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former [[:en:Musashi Province|Musashi Province]] ([[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]] and [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]]) but from throughout the entire [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto Area]]. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|qq=|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]’s [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in [[:en:1907|1907]] (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

File:Road to Musashi Dairokuten Jinja.JPG|The road leading to this shrine (with river fish restaurants)
</gallery>

== Transportation Access ==
* A 13‑minute walk from the [[:en:Transit bus|Route Bus]] stop at {{ill|Oodo Bus Stop|ja|大戸停留所|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oodo Bus Stop|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.

During the period of [[:en:Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]], this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|qq=|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in [[:en:1782|1782]] (the 2nd year of the [[:en:Tenmei|Tenmei Era]]). However, even before that it existed as a [[:en:Hokora|hokora]], and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku Period]] it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the [[:en:Ōta clan|Ota Clan]].<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its [[:en:Merit (Buddhism)|Benefit]] extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former [[:en:Musashi Province|Musashi Province]] ([[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]] and [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]]) but from throughout the entire [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto Area]]. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|qq=|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]’s [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in [[:en:1907|1907]] (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]], [[:en:Saitama (city)|Saitama City]], [[:en:Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|Iwatsuki Ward]].
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. 

== History ==
During the period of [[:en:Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]], this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in [[:en:1782|1782]] (the 2nd year of the [[:en:Tenmei|Tenmei Era]]). However, even before that it existed as a [[:en:Hokora|hokora]], and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku Period]] it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the [[:en:Ōta clan|Ota Clan]].<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its [[:en:Merit (Buddhism)|Benefit]] extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former [[:en:Musashi Province|Musashi Province]] ([[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]] and [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]]) but from throughout the entire [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto Area]]. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]’s [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in [[:en:1907|1907]] (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

File:Road to Musashi Dairokuten Jinja.JPG|The road leading to this shrine (with river fish restaurants)
</gallery>

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]], [[:en:Saitama (city)|Saitama City]], [[:en:Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|Iwatsuki Ward]].
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. 

== History ==
During the period of [[:en:Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]], this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in [[:en:1782|1782]] (the 2nd year of the [[:en:Tenmei|Tenmei Era]]). However, even before that it existed as a [[:en:Hokora|hokora]], and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku Period]] it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the [[:en:Ōta clan|Ota Clan]].<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its [[:en:Merit (Buddhism)|Benefit]] extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former [[:en:Musashi Province|Musashi Province]] ([[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]] and [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]]) but from throughout the entire [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto Area]]. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]’s [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in [[:en:1907|1907]] (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

File:Road to Musashi Dairokuten Jinja.JPG|The road leading to this shrine (with river fish restaurants)
</gallery>

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]], [[:en:Saitama (city)|Saitama City]], [[:en:Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|Iwatsuki Ward]].
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively.

During the period of [[:en:Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]], this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in [[:en:1782|1782]] (the 2nd year of the [[:en:Tenmei|Tenmei Era]]). However, even before that it existed as a [[:en:Hokora|hokora]], and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku Period]] it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the [[:en:Ōta clan|Ota Clan]].<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its [[:en:Merit (Buddhism)|Benefit]] extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former [[:en:Musashi Province|Musashi Province]] ([[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]] and [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]]) but from throughout the entire [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto Area]]. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]’s [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in [[:en:1907|1907]] (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]], [[:en:Saitama (city)|Saitama City]], [[:en:Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|Iwatsuki Ward]].
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. 

== History ==
During the period of [[:en:Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]], this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in [[:en:1782|1782]] (the 2nd year of the [[:en:Tenmei|Tenmei Era]]). However, even before that it existed as a [[:en:Hokora|hokora]], and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku Period]] it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the [[:en:Ōta clan|Ota Clan]].<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its [[:en:Merit (Buddhism)|Benefit]] extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former [[:en:Musashi Province|Musashi Province]] ([[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]] and [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]]) but from throughout the entire [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto Area]]. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]’s [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in [[:en:1907|1907]] (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]], [[:en:Saitama (city)|Saitama City]], [[:en:Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|Iwatsuki Ward]].
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. 

== History ==
During the period of [[:en:Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]], this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in [[:en:1782|1782]] (the 2nd year of the [[:en:Tenmei|Tenmei Era]]). However, even before that it existed as a [[:en:Hokora|hokora]], and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku Period]] it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the [[:en:Ōta clan|Ota Clan]].<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its [[:en:Merit (Buddhism)|Benefit]] extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former [[:en:Musashi Province|Musashi Province]] ([[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]] and [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]]) but from throughout the entire [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto Area]]. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]’s [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in [[:en:1907|1907]] (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

During the period of [[:en:Shinbutsu-shūgō|Shinbutsu-shūgō]], this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in [[:en:1782|1782]] (the 2nd year of the [[:en:Tenmei|Tenmei Era]]). However, even before that it existed as a [[:en:Hokora|hokora]], and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku Period]] it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the [[:en:Ōta clan|Ota Clan]].<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its [[:en:Merit (Buddhism)|Benefit]] extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former [[:en:Musashi Province|Musashi Province]] ([[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]] and [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]]) but from throughout the entire [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto Area]]. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]’s [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in [[:en:1907|1907]] (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Jingu|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}, {{ill|Saitama (city)|en|Saitama (city)|WD=Q134635|lt=Saitama City}}, {{ill|Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|en|Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|WD=Q1184508|lt=Iwatsuki Ward}}.
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. 

== History ==
During the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|WD=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}, this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in {{ill|1782|en|1782|WD=Q7740|lt=1782}} (the 2nd year of the {{ill|Tenmei|en|Tenmei|WD=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei Era}}). However, even before that it existed as a {{ill|Hokora|en|Hokora|WD=Q1442984|lt=hokora}}, and during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|WD=Q204023|lt=Sengoku Period}} it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the {{ill|Ōta clan|en|Ōta clan|WD=Q1391922|lt=Ota Clan}}.<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its {{ill|Merit (Buddhism)|en|Merit (Buddhism)|WD=Q1406348|lt=Benefit}} extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|WD=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province}} ({{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}} and {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo Metropolis}}) but from throughout the entire {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto Area}}. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}’s {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}, {{ill|Saitama (city)|en|Saitama (city)|WD=Q134635|lt=Saitama City}}, {{ill|Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|en|Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|WD=Q1184508|lt=Iwatsuki Ward}}.
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. 

== History ==
During the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|WD=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}, this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in {{ill|1782|en|1782|WD=Q7740|lt=1782}} (the 2nd year of the {{ill|Tenmei|en|Tenmei|WD=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei Era}}). However, even before that it existed as a {{ill|Hokora|en|Hokora|WD=Q1442984|lt=hokora}}, and during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|WD=Q204023|lt=Sengoku Period}} it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the {{ill|Ōta clan|en|Ōta clan|WD=Q1391922|lt=Ota Clan}}.<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its {{ill|Merit (Buddhism)|en|Merit (Buddhism)|WD=Q1406348|lt=Benefit}} extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|WD=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province}} ({{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}} and {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo Metropolis}}) but from throughout the entire {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto Area}}. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}’s {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

During the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|WD=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}, this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Paranimmitavasavatti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in {{ill|1782|en|1782|WD=Q7740|lt=1782}} (the 2nd year of the {{ill|Tenmei|en|Tenmei|WD=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei Era}}). However, even before that it existed as a {{ill|Hokora|en|Hokora|WD=Q1442984|lt=hokora}}, and during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|WD=Q204023|lt=Sengoku Period}} it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the {{ill|Ōta clan|en|Ōta clan|WD=Q1391922|lt=Ota Clan}}.<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its {{ill|Merit (Buddhism)|en|Merit (Buddhism)|WD=Q1406348|lt=Benefit}} extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|WD=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province}} ({{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}} and {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo Metropolis}}) but from throughout the entire {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto Area}}. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}’s {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907}} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>

'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture|1=Saitama Prefecture}}, {{ill|Saitama (city)|en|Saitama (city)|WD=Q134635|lt=Saitama City|1=Saitama (city)}}, {{ill|Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|en|Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|WD=Q1184508|lt=Iwatsuki Ward|1=Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama}}.
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively.

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=Saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

However, in {{ill|1907|en|1907|WD=Q2048|lt=1907|1=1907}} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>
