'''Musashi Dairokuten Shrine''' (武蔵第六天神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture|1=Saitama Prefecture}}, {{ill|Saitama (city)|en|Saitama (city)|qid=Q134635|lt=Saitama City|1=Saitama (city)}}, {{ill|Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|en|Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama|qid=Q1184508|lt=Iwatsuki Ward|1=Iwatsuki-ku, Saitama}}.
{{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|qq=}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. 

== History ==
During the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō|1=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}, this shrine was one of the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|ja|第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Deity Shrine|1=Dairokuten Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11602399}} that enshrined the {{ill|Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja|第六天魔王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sixth Heavenly Demon King|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天魔|1=Demon King of the Sixth Heaven|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q13578873}} ({{ill|Tataka Jizaiten|ja|他化自在天|1=Takijizaiten|2=ja|3=Takijizaiten|4=zh|5=他化自在天|6=th|7=ปรนิมมิตวสวัตดี|8=ru|9=Паринимитра-вашавартин|10=ပရနိမ္မိတဝသဝတ္တီဘုံ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tataka Jizaiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}), and was founded in {{ill|1782|en|1782|qid=Q7740|lt=1782|1=1782}} (the 2nd year of the {{ill|Tenmei|en|Tenmei|qid=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei Era|1=Tenmei}}). However, even before that it existed as a {{ill|Hokora|en|Hokora|qid=Q1442984|lt=hokora|1=Hokora}}, and during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku Period|1=Sengoku period}} it attracted the faith of local residents, including the lords of the {{ill|Ōta clan|en|Ōta clan|qid=Q1391922|lt=Ota Clan|1=Ōta clan}}.<ref name="Atsha">[https://dairokuten.or.jp/yuisho/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|History|ja|御由緒|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/History|qq=}}] {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|qq=}}</ref>

This shrine is believed to dispel all misfortunes and to ensure the safety of the household and abundant harvests. Because its {{ill|Merit (Buddhism)|en|Merit (Buddhism)|qid=Q1406348|lt=Benefit|1=Merit (Buddhism)}} extend over a wide range, many pilgrims visit not only from the former {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province|1=Musashi Province}} ({{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture|1=Saitama Prefecture}} and {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|qid=Q1490|lt=Tokyo Metropolis|1=Tokyo}}) but from throughout the entire {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|qid=Q132480|lt=Kanto Area|1=Kantō region}}. In addition, due to the enshrined deity’s “{{ill|Enshrined Deity|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enshrined Deity|1=Saijin|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11591100}}” known as “Men'''ash'''ison”, which is venerated as a god who cures foot ailments, the shrine has also recently come to be regarded as a guardian of [[:en:Road traffic safety|Traffic Safety]].<ref name="Atsha"></ref><ref name="Sanpo">Oomura, Susumu, 『Saitama Furusato Sanpo (Iwatsuki City)』, Sakitama Shuppankai, 1992, 111p</ref>

Under the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}’s {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qid=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, the shrine was originally classified as a “mukaku-sha” (unranked shrine). However, in {{ill|1907|en|1907|qid=Q2048|lt=1907|1=1907}} (the 40th year of the Meiji Era), four shrines—including the village shrine {{ill|Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Jingū|lt=Katori Shrine|ja|香取神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katori Shrine|qq=}}—were enshrined together, and it became a village shrine.<ref name="Atsha"></ref>

Because many pilgrims visit, there are many restaurants serving river fish dishes in the vicinity of this shrine.<ref name="Sanpo"></ref>
